title: Almond milk vs. oat milk: nutrition differences

seo.title: Almond milk vs. oat milk: calories, protein and calcium

seo.search_intent: Compare almond milk and oat milk nutrition

content_html:
Almond milk and oat milk may look interchangeable in coffee, but the ingredient named on the carton tells only part of the nutrition story. In current U.S. unsweetened examples, Silk Unsweet Almondmilk has 30 calories and 1 g protein per cup; Oatly Unsweetened has 40 calories and 0 g protein. Both are low-protein beverages, and much of their calcium comes from fortification.

One cup side by side

Silk Unsweet AlmondOatly Unsweetened
Calories3040
Protein1 g0 g
Fat3 g1.5 g
Carbohydrate1 g6 g
Calcium470 mg320 mg
Vitamin D4 mcg4 mcg

The calorie gap is only 10 calories per cup. The larger macro difference is carbohydrate: 6 g in the oat drink versus 1 g in almond milk. Protein is negligible in both.

Neither drink reproduces the nutrition of its whole ingredient

A handful of almonds is rich in fat, fiber, and protein, but almond milk is mostly water and is filtered and formulated to behave like a beverage. Likewise, oat milk does not contain the same concentration of fiber and protein as a bowl of oats.

That is why judging these drinks by the reputation of almonds or oats can be misleading. The finished label matters.

Fortification explains much of the calcium

Silk lists 470 mg calcium per cup and Oatly 320 mg. Both provide 4 mcg vitamin D. Those nutrients are added during manufacturing rather than reflecting a direct transfer from a handful of almonds or a serving of oats.

Fortification varies between brands and product lines, so another almond or oat milk may be much lower. Shake fortified beverages as directed because minerals can settle.

Oat milk has more carbohydrate in this example

Oatly Unsweetened provides 6 g carbohydrate per cup compared with 1 g in the Silk almond drink. Both products are unsweetened, which shows why “unsweetened” and “carbohydrate-free” are not the same thing.

Protein is the weak point for both

One cup provides 1 g protein in almond milk and 0 g in this oat milk. If the beverage is replacing dairy milk as a regular protein source, a higher-protein product—often soy milk—may be a closer nutritional substitute.

Which should you choose?

Choose unsweetened almond milk for a very low-calorie, low-carbohydrate option and oat milk for a different body and flavor profile. Neither product is a meaningful protein source. For calcium, vitamin D, or B12, compare the exact fortified label rather than assuming one plant base always provides more.

faq.answer: Almond in these examples: 30 versus 40 calories per cup.

faq.answer: The almond example has 1 g versus 0 g; both are low.

faq.question: Is the calcium natural?
faq.answer: Much of it is added through fortification.
